protocol_md:
## Protocol

Precommitted before this sample was scored:

- Sample: first SPY session on or after 2000-01-03 through the last available session. The SMA may use earlier history. The T-bill input is the 13-week yield (`^IRX`), lagged one session, divided by 100 and by 252.
- Execution: the signal is fixed at the close and filled at the next open. Cash earns the lagged T-bill. SPY, SSO, and UPRO pay 5 bps one-way. Cash does not pay a spread in the base case.
- Leveraged sleeve: daily reset, `r_L = L * r - (L - 1) * (rf + 0.40% / 252) - ER / 252`, with expense ratios 0.89% (SSO) and 0.91% (UPRO). The synthetic open gaps by L times the underlying overnight move. Financing and the expense ratio sit in the rest of the close-to-close return.
- Grid, and every cell is a trial: leverage 2 and 3; sleeve weight 30, 40, 50, 60, and 70 percent; filters SMA 200 daily, SMA 200 daily with a 2% band, SMA 200 evaluated monthly, SMA 150 daily, and SMA 100 daily with a 2% band; mix reset monthly and quarterly. Plus a 100% sleeve for leverage 2 and 3 (the mix reset does nothing when the core weight is zero, so it is stored once). Plus unlevered sleeves of 50% and 100% on the same filters, monthly and quarterly.
- The desk's 50/50 UPRO mix is one of those cells: SMA 200, a 2% hysteresis band (enter when the close is above 1.02 times the average, exit only when it is below 0.98 times, hold the previous state in between), daily filter, quarterly mix. The desk chose that weight after seeing results. This study reports the cell as pre-specified. It does not crown it from the full-sample Sharpe.
- Walk-forward: on the first session of each year from 2006, pick the cell with the highest excess Sharpe versus T-bills using only returns strictly before that session, requiring 756 prior sessions. Ties break alphabetically. The stitched path is the out-of-sample record. It is compared with SPY over those same sessions, not with SPY from 2000.
- The live trend-core book is that 50/50 cell plus a dip overlay on the SPY half only. After three strictly down SPY closes, that half is SSO instead of SPY until the next open after the first up close or the fifth session, whichever comes first. The UPRO half is not resized by the dip. The other dip rules (two-day -2%, two-day -3%, three-day -3%, three-day -4%) are the same overlay on the same 50/50 book, and each rule is a trial.
- Buy-and-hold synthetic SSO and UPRO are trials. Buy-and-hold SPY is the benchmark and is not a trial. Cost and next-close reruns are recorded as audits and do not increment N.
- The walk-forward edge survives only if its CAGR exceeds buy-and-hold SPY over the same sessions (first decision date through the sample end), its information-ratio t-stat exceeds the expected maximum of N independent standard normals, and its deflated Sharpe ratio is at least 0.95. N and the Sharpe dispersion come from the persistent ledger.
- If that bar is cleared, the live book is the variant selected for the current year. If the path beats SPY but misses the bar, the edge does not survive; the flagship file still shows the rule's current weights and is marked not endorsed. If the path does not beat SPY, the recommendation is 100% SPY.
caveats: Synthetic 3x/2x returns before the ETF listing are a model. The overlap table is the check. Real swap spreads, dividend treatment inside the fund, and creation/redemption can differ from `ER` plus 40 bps over T-bills.
The multiple-testing bar treats trials as independent. These variants share one market, so the bar is conservative and a miss is informative. A pass would be more fragile than the formula suggests.
The 50/50 weight was the desk's post-hoc choice. It is inside the grid so it is counted. It is not re-selected on the full sample.
Block bootstrap redraws historical daily returns. It does not invent a new regime, and it ignores taxes. Trend and dip exits are mostly short-term gains in a taxable account.

A consumer that rebalances to `weights` every session implements the daily-reset mix, not the quarterly drift. `trade` and `rebalance_mix` say when the lower-turnover book would actually trade. `signals.json` is the fixed trend-core book, including the dip overlay on the SPY half. The flagship file is written by the separate return-max study.
This is research on public prices. It is not a recommendation to buy leveraged ETFs.

iterations.title: Credit-spread sleeve hedge
iterations.hypothesis: The live book keeps the 3x sleeve on until SPY closes through its 200-day band. That lag is the weakness in the refreshed subperiod table: the trend-core book trails SPY in 2020 and again in 2022. A widening credit spread is a faster stress signal. When the 20-session change in the spread exceeds a precommitted threshold, move only the leveraged sleeve to T-bills. The SPY core, the three-down-close dip, and the quarterly mix are unchanged. The sleeve goes back to UPRO when the trend is on and the 20-session widening is back at or below the threshold.

iterations.title: Volatility-scaled UPRO sleeve
iterations.hypothesis: The trend core's maximum drawdown is about -46.8% because the 200-day band keeps the 3x sleeve invested through the first leg of a crash. Trailing realized volatility of SPY rises in that window, before the slow average turns. Scale only the UPRO sleeve to min(1, target_vol / trailing sample volatility), using a close-to-close window known at the signal close and filled at the next open. The rest of the sleeve budget earns T-bills. The SPY core, the three-down-close dip, and the quarterly mix are unchanged. The scale is capped at 1. The grid is lookbacks 10, 21, and 63 sessions and target volatilities 10%, 15%, 20%, and 25%, fixed before this sample is scored. The walk-forward may also select the unscaled book. The stitched path is kept only when it clears the materiality bar.

iterations.title: Multi-lookback vote on the UPRO sleeve
iterations.hypothesis: The live sleeve stays on until SPY closes through its 200-day band. That lag is why the trend-core drawdown is still about -46.8%, and why the book trailed SPY in 2020 and 2022. The 2026-10-26 volatility scale cut the sleeve whenever realized volatility was high, including in high-vol rallies, so the stitched path gained 2.6 drawdown points (short of 3) and the daily improvement had a negative Sharpe. A multi-lookback vote turns the sleeve off only when shorter trend states have broken, and it requires agreement before the sleeve is on. Each lookback uses the same hysteresis as the live filter. The grid is short windows 50 and 100 (middles 100 and 150, long window fixed at 200), minimum votes 2 and 3, and bands 0 and 2%, fixed before this sample is scored. The single-window grid already contains SMA 100, 150, and 200 on their own; it does not contain this vote. The SPY core, the three-down-close dip, and the quarterly mix are unchanged. The walk-forward may also select the current 200-day band. The stitched path is kept only when it clears the materiality bar.

iterations.title: Trailing-peak stop on the UPRO sleeve
iterations.hypothesis: The live sleeve stays on until SPY closes through its 200-day band. That lag is why the trend-core drawdown is still about -46.8%, and why the book trailed SPY in 2020 and 2022. The 2026-10-26 volatility scale cut the sleeve whenever realized volatility was high, including in high-vol rallies, and gained 2.6 drawdown points, short of 3, with a negative improvement Sharpe. The 2026-10-27 multi-lookback vote was never selected, so the stitched path matched the current book, and the vote cells themselves had deeper drawdowns. A trailing-peak stop cuts only the UPRO sleeve after SPY has already fallen from its own high, so a high-vol rally that is still near that high stays invested. The peak is the maximum close over 63, 126, or 252 sessions. The sleeve goes to T-bills when the close is 8%, 12%, or 16% below that peak, and it returns when the drawdown has healed to half the cut and the 200-day trend is still on. The half-cut re-entry is fixed, not a searched axis. The single-window grid already contains SMA 100, 150, and 200; this stop does not replace that filter. The SPY core, the three-down-close dip, and the quarterly mix are unchanged. The walk-forward may also select the current book. The stitched path is kept only when it clears the materiality bar.
